system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: CIRT NCT01594333 - Cardiovascular Inflammation Reduction Trial
Investigational drug: methotrexate
Document: Long-term survival results of a randomized trial comparing gemcitabine plus cisplatin, with methotrexate, vinblastine, doxorubicin, plus cisplatin in patients with bladder cancer. (journal, published 2005-07-01, source pmid:16034041)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
Long-term survival results of a randomized trial comparing gemcitabine plus cisplatin, with methotrexate, vinblastine, doxorubicin, plus cisplatin in patients with bladder cancer.

Purpose To compare long-term survival in patients with locally advanced or metastatic transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) of the urothelium treated with gemcitabine/cisplatin (GC) or methotrexate/vinblastine/doxorubicin/cisplatin (MVAC). Patients and methods Efficacy data from a large randomized phase III study of GC versus MVAC were updated. Time-to-event analyses were performed on the observed distributions of overall and progression-free survival. Results A total of 405 patients were randomly assigned: 203 to the GC arm and 202 to the MVAC arm. At the time of analysis, 347 patients had died (GC arm, 176 patients; MVAC arm, 171 patients). Overall survival was similar in both arms (hazard ratio [HR], 1.09; 95% CI, 0.88 to 1.34; P = .66) with a median survival of 14.0 months for GC and 15.2 months for MVAC. The 5-year overall survival rates were 13.0% and 15.3%, respectively (P = .53). The median progression-free survival was 7.7 months for GC and 8.3 months for MVAC, with an HR of 1.09. The 5-year progression-free survival rates were 9.8% and 11.3%, respectively (P = .63). Significant prognostic factors favoring overall survival included performance score (> 70), TNM staging (M0 v M1), low/normal alkaline phosphatase level, number of disease sites ( Conclusion Long-term overall and progression-free survival after treatment with GC or MVAC are similar. These results strengthen the role of GC as a standard of care in patients with locally advanced or metastatic TCC.
--- END ---
